(1) Oṃ, salutations to the illustrious (3) Mahāgaṇeśa. Salutations to the sandals of the illustrious Guru.
[Then follows the ritual procedure for the worship of the pedestal.]

To the petitioner for the flower-vessel of the sacrificer: From this day forward, the formula: For the sake of pleasing the venerable Ākāśa-Mahābhairava, [this is] the consecration of the chariot of the sacrificer, Mānavagotra Śrī-Śrī-Jayabhūpatīndramallavarman, together with the hoisting of the golden pinnacle and banner upon it, and the Bhairava-fire ritual.
I offer this vessel of flowers for the purpose of performing the worship of the Eight Mothers as a sacrifice of one thousand oblations performed day and night.
Within the mandala of Śrī Saṃvartā, there is the most formidable power of bliss accompanied by the sequential steps;
the fourfold group is emitted according to the rule, as well as another fivefold group belonging to the Kula and Akula, and a sixfold group.
Furthermore, there are four others, and again another four; this is the mandala according to its true nature.
Bow down to that excellent Guru, Śrī Kujeśa, with whom Bhairava is united.

Dark-complexioned, red-hued, with three eyes, bent by the weight of her breasts, walking with the gait of an elephant in rut, with lips like the *bimba* fruit, beautiful eyes, broad palms and hips, radiant with the jewels of her girdle,
adorned with divine garments and exquisite flowers, and possessing a mass of hair of deep golden hue.
May she, known as the glorious Kubjikā, who is full of vital energy, bestow upon me the unfailing enjoyment of the divine flood of knowledge.
Seated upon the pericarp of a full-blown lotus, she is the supreme Śrī Siddhilakṣmī,
white as camphor, crystal, and the moon, who removes every trace of sin.
May she who burns away the suffering of the ocean of saṃsāra, who is forever unshakable, whose glorious five lotus-faces and ten arms are radiant, and who stands upon a corpse, protect you.
Fair-complexioned, possessing the splendor of three eyes, with five faces, seated upon a lion, he is the Attractor;

holding a noose, a mallet, a sword, a rosary, and the gesture of fearlessness; the Lord of Serpents, dark-brown in hue, with a vessel filled with sweetmeats and bestowing fearlessness, his right hands likewise hold these implements.
Salutations to Helāmbanātha, who is captivating with his trident, possesses a magnificent belly, and is the lord of sport.
Brahmāṇī, with a face as gentle as a lotus and the moon; Māheśvarī, who by her play destroys the pride of enemies; Kaumārī, whose weapon is the discus; Vaiṣṇavī;
Vārāhī, with a snout as terrible and rumbling as a thundercloud; and Aindrī, whose weapon is the thunderbolt.
May Cāmuṇḍā, Gaṇanātha, Bhairava, and the hosts of Mothers protect me.
I always worship the Goddess Sundarī, who dwells in the center of the sacred seat (pīṭha), seated upon a corpse (pretāsana), red-limbed, holding a trident and a skull-bowl,
the bestower of the essence of worldly existence, and ever adored by Brahmā, Upendra, the Lord of the Gods, and hosts of Kinnaras.
I praise her and bow my head perpetually to her, the bestower of the fulfillment of desires and goals.
The Yoginī, surrounded by Brahmāṇī and others such as Jayā, resides in the sacred field (kṣetra);
she is of one flavor with all the gods in Śrīvīra, holding a trident and a rosary;
she is Unmattā, bearing the auspicious weapons of Sāṅka, and is enveloped in streams of nectar.
Oṃ, salutations to you, the Mistress of the Cakra, accompanied by the Bindu and the syllables beginning with *pra* which conceal passion (*premā*).

To the east, south, west, and north are the auspicious ones; in the directions starting from the east, they are Vāmāsikā, Kṣetreśa, Vaṭu, Bhūta, Durgā, and Haraṇa, as well as Helambanātha. To the Lord of the Cremation Ground (Śmaśāneśvara), the primordial deity, who has two arms, [I offer salutations] for the removal of defects such as sorrow.
The ritual procedure for the worship of Sadāvalī and others, consisting of eternal bliss, performed with joy.
May there be success at the commencement of your undertakings; may there be prosperity upon the arrival of wealth;
may there be nourishment for your bodies, and may there be peace in your home.
It pacifies all obstacles, brings about all peace, and is auspicious;
it increases longevity, desire, fortune, and progeny.
Just as armor is the warder-off of blows from weapons,
so too let peace be the warder-off of the acts of the Creator.
I offer this vessel of flowers.
When the cow [is] raw, [and] the milk-pot is not heated; if these are not stirred, the butter will solidify.
The removal of obstacles, the offering of oblations, and the union of the arms at the fall of the oblation—this is the couplet (5). The nine oblations (5).
The skillful one, possessing the vessel of worship, is bowed down by the assembly of sages. Kevophaṃ. (1)
Bathing and so forth; for the purpose of painting the body.
The syllable *ū* is the seed-syllable of Vāyu; above that is Varuṇa and Vajrapāṇi;

above that is Kāla joined with the final letter of the alphabet; above that is the supreme seed-syllable of Fire, together with *haṃsa*, the lunar drop (*bindu*), and the end of dissolution—bearing a white lotus and flowing with streams of milk.
Having seen a fraud, one constantly burns his family; for such sin is indeed equal to Mount Meru.
The ritual bath for the eyebrows.
ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ, the venerable pādukā. If [it is] so.
May this divine sandalwood paste from Śrīkhaṇḍa, rich in fragrance and most enchanting,
adorned with a mark upon the forehead, be accepted.
Sandalwood paste is meritorious, purifying, and a destroyer of evil;
it constantly removes calamities and bestows fortune, sovereignty, and happiness.
Sindūra (vermilion)
Vīreśvarī, the Great Heroine, is adorned with the ashes of heroes;
she is the Goddess who attracts the three worlds, most excellent and crimson as vermilion.
Unbroken.
O unbroken and inexhaustible one, who grants the fulfillment of the aims of dharma, desire, and wealth—
grant me my desired boon, and in the next world, the supreme goal.
View.
Please accept this pair of spectacles, which reveals the fourteen worlds— Heaven, Earth, and the single Pātāla— for the sake of attaining the fruit of divine vision.
The performers of sacrifice.
May that sacred thread (*yajñopavīta*)— the supreme purifier, which was born together with Prajāpati in the beginning,
which bestows long life, is foremost, and is auspicious— be yours as the highest.
Or else, at the door.
O you who pervade the entire world, accept this garment made of cotton, which is supremely purifying and bestows happiness and prosperity; salutations to you!
Svāna.
O auspicious lady, this supreme ritual of offering flowers is rich with the fragrance of various blossoms, resembles the *mālatī* flower, and bestows the attainment of good fortune.
The Ear-flag.
Having taken a very beautiful four-cornered flagstaff named Karṇa, which has the luster of pure vermilion, one should take up the supreme lords.
The five banners.
O Goddess, accept this pair of earrings for the sake of [my] ears, this five-colored banner,
and this excellent flag for the sake of attaining the fruit of the five siddhis.
In Caphumāḍha.
O Lord of Gods, by the gift of this divine parasol, which is like a wish-fulfilling gem and shines like the full moon, grant me the fruit I have desired.
The worship of the *mālaka* with the *japa*. The sipping of water (*ācamana*) by means of the three truths (*tritatva*).
Hrāṃ, svāhā to the principle of the Self (ātmatattva). Hrīṃ, svāhā to the principle of knowledge (vidyātattva). Hūṃ, svāhā to the principle of Śiva (śivatattva).
Hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ, svāhā to all the principles (tattvas).
The Sun’s Arghya Offering: [Recite] the formula beginning with "Today and so forth... [and] the introductory statement.
Having extracted the seed-syllable ending with the letter *va*, one should place *śiva* above it;
it is adorned by the three fires at its beginning, middle, and end.
Having illuminated it with the *varman*, one should indeed extract the *Sāvitrī*.
This is the most excellent and supreme *kūṭa*, the Great Mārtaṇḍa-Bhairava.
Argha, obeisance! Flower, obeisance! Rhrkṣrīṁ, obeisance to Śrī Mahāmārttaṇḍa Bhairava.
[Guru-namaskāra.]
aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hsphreṃ hsauṃ ||
Salutation to that illustrious Guru by whom that state was revealed— the state which is of the nature of an unbroken circle and by which the moving and the unmoving are pervaded.
The Guru is Brahmā, the Guru is Viṣṇu, the Guru is the Lord Maheśvara;
the Guru is the God who is the entire universe—salutations to that glorious Guru.
Salutations to the supreme gurus. Salutations to the gurus who are the Parameṣṭhins. Salutations to the gurus who are the supreme teachers.
The lotus stalk.
The sandals for the lotus posture.
Thavake || Pādukā for Kūrmmāsana.
On the side is the rite for scattering unbroken rice: *Kiṇi vicce koṅkaṇāyai hraḥ astrāya phaṭ*.
Binding the face with the vajra-mudrā: Aiṃ (5) Hūṃ Phaṭ Vajrapañjare Svāhā.
The touching of the ten gates: (5) *cale me kule akule hrīṃ hrūṃ phaṭ svāhā*.
The ritual placement (nyāsa).
(5) Kiṇi (2), Vicce Koṅkaṇāyai Hraḥ Astrāya Phaṭ, [worship] the sandals.
The purification of the hands (4).

Homage to the Blessed Lady Hṛtkamalā! Hrāṃ Śrī! Sandals for the two thumbs! Hsphreṃ! To Kubjikā, the Lamp of the Kula! Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! Sandals for the two index fingers! (5) Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ! O Varvarashikhā! Hrūṃ! Sandals for the two middle fingers! (5) Ghore Aghore...

To Aghorāmukhī Vahurūpā, *hraim śrīm*, [I offer] the sandals to the two ring fingers. (5) To Mahantārikā, *chām chīm*, *hraum śrīṃ*, [I offer] the sandals to the two little fingers. (5) *Kiṇi (2) vicce*, to Koṅkaṇā, *hraḥ śrīṃ*, [I offer] the sandals to the backs of both hands. Thus is the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the hands.

(5) Homage to the Blessed One, the Lotus of the Heart, the Glorious One with the Upward-Facing Face; [I offer] the sandals. (5) Hsphreṁ! To Kubjikā, the Lamp of the Kula, the Glorious One with the Front-Facing Face; [I offer] the sandals. (5) Hrāṁ Hrīṁ Hrūṁ! To Varvarashikhā...

The sandals for the venerable Southern Face. (5) Ghore aghore aghorāmukhi bahurūpāyai, the sandals for the venerable Northern Face. (5) Chāṃ chīṃ mahantārikāyai, the sandals for the venerable Western Face. (5) Kiṇi (2) vicce koṅkaṇāyai, the sandals for the venerable Parāpara Face. Thus.
The ritual placement on the mouth (*vaktranyāsa*).

(5) Homage to the Blessed Lady Hṛtkamalā; *hrāṃ*, to the heart, the sandals. (5) *Hsphreṃ*, to Kubjikā, the lamp of the Kula; *hrīṃ*, to the head, *svāhā*. (5) *Hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ*, O you with the dark-blue crest! *Hrūṃ*, to the glorious crest, *vauṣaṭ*. (5) *Ghore aghore aghorāmukhi bahurūpāyai*, *hraim*, to the armor.
Hūṃ! Chāṃ chīṃ, vaṣaṭ to the three eyes of Mahantārikā! Hrauṃ! Vaṣaṭ!
(5) *Kiṇi* (2), *vicce*, to Koṅkaṇā, *hraḥ*, to the weapon (*astra*), *phaṭ*. Thus is the ritual placement on the limbs (*aṅganyāsa*).

The sandals for the seat of the water-vessel: Aiṃ (5) Hskṣmlvryūṃ, to the face of Ānandaśaktibhairava, the sovereign of heroes, Śkṣmlvryīṃ, the sandals for the venerable Śrījalapātrabhaṭṭārikā. Hrāṃ, salutation to the heart; Hrīṃ, svāhā to the head; Hūṃ, vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock; Hraiṃ, hūṃ to the armor.
Hrauṃ, vaṣaṭ to the three eyes; Hraḥ, phaṭ to the weapon. [Perform] the invocation and other rites; [form] the dhenumudrā.
Gāyatrī.
Aiṃ (5). We know Kubjikā; we meditate upon her, the lamp of the Kula; may that Kubjī inspire us.
The worship of the argha vessel.

The sandals for the seat of the Argha vessel: Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ Hraḥ Prasphura (2) Ghora (2) Taratanu (2) Rūpacaṭa (2) Pracaṭa (2) Kaha (2) Vama (2) Dama (2) Ghātaya (2) Vighātaya (2) Vighni (2) Hūṃ (3) Phaṭ Kroṃ Śrīmahākaumārikā Vicce, the sandals.

Aiṃ (5) ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ Ānandaśaktibhairavānanda Śrīmahāvidyārājeśvarī HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ. [Salutation] to the venerable Arghapātrabhaṭṭārikā, the sandals. [The six limbs. Having invoked, [one should form] the Yonimudrā.
Purification of the Elements (Bhūtaśuddhi)
aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hsphreṃ hsauṃ hsauṃ hsphreṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ ||
Self-worship.
Aiṁ, sandalwood, the sandals. Hrīṁ, unbroken rice grains, the sandals. Śrī Vīrabhasma, the sandals.

Hsphreṃ, the sandals of the Enchantress of All People. Hsauṃ, the sandals of the various parasols, ornaments, and flowers. Aiṃ (5) Hskṣmlvryūṃ, to the Lord of Heroes, Ānanda, who is the Bliss of Bhairava and the Power of Ānanda;
Śkṣmlvryīṃ, to the Self, flowers and the sandals. Aiṃ Kusau, the sandals. The three points (3).
Thus ends the self-worship.
One should recite the Mālinī-daṇḍaka: Oṃ, salutation to Caṇḍikā.
The illustrious Bhairava said:
Aiṃ (5). May the goddess Mālinī be victorious! You are stainless, the destroyer of impurity;
you are the goddess born of the power of knowledge (*jñānaśakti*), the intellect (*buddhi*), and the increaser of splendor.
The mother of all beings, established in this saṃsāra, is the goddess Mātāvīrāvalī; O compassionate one, O affectionate mother, have mercy!

Victorious is You, the supreme power of transcendental knowledge (*parājñānaśakti*), born from the manifestation of the ultimate reality of Nirvāṇa, consisting of light, and having emerged in manifest form. You are the auspicious powers of Will (*icchā*) and Action (*kriyā*). Furthermore, You are praised as the radiant power of Sound (*nādaśakti*), appearing as a straight line, a beautiful curve, and again in the form of a coil like a sleeping lord of serpents.

You are the form of light, the essential nature, named Jyeṣṭhā of Śiva, as well as Vāmā, Raudrī, and Manonmanī; you are the form of the Bindu, the daughter-in-law (Vadhūtā), and the shape of the half-moon; you are the triangle, the combination of the letters A, U, Ma, O, and Ī, unified as one; you are the primordial source, the embodiment of reality, abiding in the form of the Bhaga from the very beginning.

She who arises from the reality of forbearance (*kṣāntatattva*), whose form is that of a womb, whose nature is her own essence, the awakener of Śrīkaṇṭha, the mother of Rudra, as well as the power of Nanda, the most subtle one, the three-formed one, the one who receives the offering (*arghinī*) of Amarīśa, Bhārabhūti, she whose self is the state of persistence (*sthiti*), and Sthāṇu.

O Bhūtāhatākṣa, Jhaṇṭhīśa, Bhautīśa, Sadyojāta, Ātmika, Anugraheśa, you who are worshipped; O Krūra, Śāṅga, Mahāsena, Sambhoginī, Ṣoḍaśāntā, Amṛtā, Bindusaṃdohinī—flow forth from this body! O you who have leaped over all that is to be pacified, O bestower of the bliss of supreme bliss and liberation, [salutations] to Bhairavī, Bhairava, and the others.
Kriḍānuśakti, Parāmāriṇī, Rudramātā, Arcitā, Rudraśakti, Khagasiddhi, Yogeśvarī, Siddhimātā, Vibhu, Śabdarāśi, Yonyārṇavī, Vāgviśuddhā, Śivāsiddhi, Vāgeśvarī,
Mātṛkāsiddhi, Ichā, Kriyā, Maṅgalāsiddhi, Lakṣmī, and Vibhūti.
You are Saṃbhūti, Gati, Śāśvatā, Khyāti, Nārāyaṇī, Raktacaṇḍā, Karālā, Kṣaṇā, Bhīmarūpā, Mahocchūṣmā, Yogapriyā, Jayantī, Ajitā, Rudrasaṃmohinī,
and you are she who rests upon the lap of the God known as Navātmā.
O Goddess, you are worshipped by mantra-following practitioners who are devoted to the drinking of heroes (vīrapāna) and filled with supreme devotion,
through the five nectars (pañcāmṛta) and festivals of divine drink; and you are honored by those born of one, two, three, four, five, six, or seven births, who have mastered the scriptures.
O you who delight in wine and meat, you are gratified by men who are auspicious yet fragile,
resplendent with mantras, sciences, and vows— by the Kālakāpālikas who wear shaven heads, who have ascended to divine conduct, and who utter the salutations *oṃ*, *svāhā*, and *svadhā*.
With the *vauṣaṭ*, *vaṣaṭ*, *huṃ*, and *phaṭ* syllables,

and by means of these mantra-syllables recited while held in the left hand— by the practitioners (*sādhaka*), sons, mothers, maṇḍalas, initiated yogins, and the assemblies of yoginīs gathered in melāpaka— protect the string of beads with these mantras.

O Yoginī, bestower of the perfection of yoga, you are worshipped by those who delight in the play of Rudra; O Goddess, with eyes like lotus petals, you look upon him with affection. Abiding in heaven and the intermediate space, moving through the seven netherworlds, your unimpeded accomplishment is described for one who recites this *Daṇḍaka* with devotion.

That man who, being pure, should always remember [the Goddess] once, twice, thrice, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine times a day— even he is protected by the Goddess from thieves, fire, weapons, the ocean, and mountain peaks, O beloved of Mahālakṣmī; she protects even those sons who are attached to passion, thieves of gold, those intent on the wives of others, and even killers of Brahmins and cows.
Even those who are corrupted by great faults release [their enmity] upon recollecting your face, O Goddess—
which resembles the full moon, where the surface of the cheeks is rubbed by excellent earrings of shimmering divine rubies—
even those whose arms and toes are bound with firm bonds and serpent-nooses.

O Goddess Mahākālī, whose splendor is like the fire of cosmic destruction (Kālāgni), whose head is adorned with a garland of bees by the crowns of Skanda, Brahmā, Indra, Candra, and Arka, and who holds the flower-weapon (the god of love)— by chanting your name and remembering your two lotus feet, people are released from terrible and great diseases.
O Mother of all heroes, O Bhairavī, whose [hair] is as tawny as the filaments of a beautiful lotus—O Śivā, I have come to you for refuge; forgive my transgression, forgive my transgression!
Having thus praised her, the Great Goddess emerged from the piercing of the *liṅga* by the high-souled Bhairava; then the Supreme Sovereign appeared.
Thus ends the Mālinī-daṇḍaka hymn.
And five rows.
Aiṃ (5) the sandals for Mayūrāsana. Aiṃ (5) Śrīṃ Hrīṃ, the sandals for Kulaputra Vaṭukanātha.
The offering.
(5) For Narāsaṇa, the sandals. Aiṃ (5) Thrauṃ. For Bhakī Devī, the Mistress of Prastaradvīpa, and for Mahādhvāṅkṣa Kṣetrapāla, the sandals.
The sacrificial offering.
(5) The sandals for the corpse-seat: Aiṃ (5) Yāṃ, the sandals for the Yoginīs.

Bali: (5) Whosoever among the Yoginīs are born of the *pīṭhas*, born of the fields (*kṣetra*), born together (*sahaja*), born of enjoyment (*joga*), born from the womb (*garbha*), or born of the lineage (*kula*); whosoever among the Yoginīs are the sky-walkers (*khecarī*), earth-walkers (*bhūcarī*), and ground-walkers (*gocarī*); those of one syllable, two syllables, three syllables, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, or ten syllables; those who move through the three paths—[to them I offer this].
Accept the offering of those who have arrived as they are; svāhā!
(5) To the seat of the pretas, the sandals! Aiṁ (5) Hskhphrīṁ, to the sandals of Śrī Siddhicāmuṇḍeśvarī!
The sacrificial offering.
(5) For the seat of the crucible, the sandals: Aiṁ. (5) Gāṁ Gīṁ Gūṁ Gaiṁ Gauṁ Gaḥ Glauṁ.
Sandals for the venerable Kulagaṇeśvara. The offering (bali).
The rites beginning with the invocation (āvāhana).
One should display the mudrās of the staff, the threatening gesture, the womb, the drop, and the elephant.
Recite.
Śrīṃ hrīṃ svāhā (10 times). Thrauṃ svāhā (10 times). Yāṃ svāhā (10 times). Hskhphreṃ svāhā (10 times).
Glauṃ svāhā.
Hymn of Praise.
[I bow to] Kumāra, the son of Gaurī, who is supported by the tree of the sky; to Kṣetrapāla and the Yoginīs;
to Cāmuṇḍā of fierce form; and to Gaṇeśa, who removes misfortune and fear and destroys obstacles.

Adorned with flowers and the like, incense, lamps, and offerings of honey and rice-gruel, her limbs beautifully decorated, she was worshipped in the center of the circle; she is the benefactor of diverse people and the bestower of both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
In this rite of worship with the five offerings, may all of that be completely fulfilled.
Invocation.

Within the mandala of the venerable Samvarta, the power of bliss is established through the sequential steps; it is auspicious, possessing the fourfold logic of emanation, as well as another fivefold set pertaining to Akula and Kula, and a sixfold set.
There are four, another fivefold set, and again four; this is that mandala.
Bow down to that excellent Guru, Śrī Kujeśa Bhairava, by whom [all things] are intermingled.
This I shall summon; I summon.
Enough, O Infinite Mandala! Enough with the sandals of the Primordial God Śrī Ādideva!
Trideva, Āsana, (5) Narāsanā, Pādukā.

(5) Pādukā to Mayūsanātha. (5) Pādukā to Mūṣāsanātha. (5) *Thrauṃ*! Pādukā to the goddess Dambhakī of Prastaradvīpa and to Mahādhvāṅkṣa Kṣetrapāla. (5) *Śrīṃ Hrīṃ*! Pādukā to Kulaputra Vaṭukanātha. *Gāṃ Gīṃ Gūṃ Gaḥ Glauṃ*.
To the Lord of the Family and the Gana, the sandals.
This is the *bali* for them. Having invoked [them], [one should display] the *tarjanī*, the *daṇḍa*, and the *gaja* mudrās.
Indra and others: *Lūṃ*, obeisance to Indra; *Baliṃ*; *Rūṃ*, obeisance to Agni; *Mūṃ*, obeisance to Yama.

KṢŪṂ, salutation to Nairṛtya. VŪṂ, salutation to Varuṇa. YŪṂ, salutation to Vāyu. SŪṂ, salutation to Kubera. HŪṂ, salutation to Īśāna. AṂ, salutation to Ananta. UṂ, salutation to Brahmā. With these, [offer] the bali.
Jayādi || The sandals for Jayā. The sandals for Vijayā. The sandals for Ajitā.
A sandal for Aparājitā; a sandal for Jambhanī.
The sandal that paralyzes. The sandal that deludes. The sandal that attracts.
This is the offering (bali) for them.

Brahmāṇy-ādi: Aṃ, the sandals of Brahmāṇī; Kaṃ, the sandals of Māheśvarī; Caṃ, the sandals of Kaumārī; Ṭaṃ, the sandals of Vaiṣṇavī; Taṃ, the sandals of Vārāhī; Paṃ, the sandals of Indrāṇī; Yaṃ, the sandals of Cāmuṇḍā; Śaṃ, [the sandals] of Mahālakṣmī.
The sandals; the offering for these is as follows.
Hetukādi. Hūṃ, homage to Hetuka Bhairava! Hūṃ, homage to Tripurāntaka Bhairava!
Hūṃ, homage to Agnijihvābhairava! Hūṃ, homage to Agnivetālabhairava! Hūṃ, homage to Kālākṣabhairava! Hūṃ, homage to Kalālibhairava! Hūṃ, homage to Ekapādabhairava! Hūṃ, homage to Bhīmarūpabhairava!

when he is thus bathed, the deities are forever well-pleased.
Ghela!
O Pinākin, you who are purified by the clarified butter and purified by the Liṅga,
[protect] that triple world and its people, auspicious as you are, in the form of fire and serpents.
Who is this?
This Gomukhī is the source of power, beloved by the gods and dear to them;
it is the bath that grants the wish-fulfilling tree, through which such a bath is obtained.
Sākhala.
This sugar-candy is exceedingly delicious and always cool to the mind;
O God, this unbroken moon-shaped candy, when bathed [with water], bestows unimpaired strength.
The five nectars.
Likewise, I bathe with the fivefold water, the resident of the five Brahmans, endowed with the five substances, using the five limbs.
Bathing of the eyebrows.

The attendant.
May this divine sandalwood paste from Śrīkhaṇḍa, whose fragrance and other qualities are captivating,
and which adorns the forehead known as the moon, be accepted.
Anointed with sandalwood paste, it is meritorious, pure, and a destroyer of sins;
it constantly removes calamities and bestows prosperity, sovereignty, and happiness.
May you attain success!
Vīreśvarī, the Great Heroine, who draws in the three worlds, is the supreme goddess, reddened with vermilion and adorned with the ashes of heroes.
Unbroken.
O Goddess, grant me my desired boon— imperishable and inexhaustible according to my wish— which bestows the accomplishment of Dharma, Kāma, and Artha, as well as the supreme goal in the hereafter.
View.
Graceful within the wide vision of meditation and the eyes of heroes,
the pure eye is the uneven world of the moon, sun, and fire.
The performers of sacrifice.
The sacred thread (*yajñopavīta*), the supreme purifier, which was born together with Prajāpati in the beginning—
may you put on this auspicious and foremost thread, which bestows long life and is the highest splendor.
Or else, the door.
O Supreme Lord, accept this divine garment, the most excellent of ornaments, adorned with various cloths and made of fine linen and cotton.
Caḍhumāḍhe.
O Lord of Gods, by the gift of this divine parasol, which is like a wish-fulfilling gem and shines like the full moon, grant me the fruit of my desire.
Bathing.
O auspicious lady, this supreme offering of flowers— consisting of various fragrant blossoms and the blooming of jasmine— is the bestower of good fortune and success.
The five banners.
This five-colored banner, hanging from the ears, consists of the five elements; made of fine linen, it bestows the five [senses].
The Ear-flag.
O Supreme Lord, accept this beautiful four-cornered banner, which has the luster of pure vermilion and is known by the name Karṇa.
May all these be auspicious!
This yellow powder is not a garland of flowers; this offering is a garland of flowers.

Hrāṃ, svāhā to the principle of the Self (ātmatattva). Hrīṃ, svāhā to the principle of knowledge (vidyātattva). Hruṃ, svāhā to the principle of Śiva (śivatattva).
The offering to the Sun (*sūryārgha*). The formula beginning with "Today and so forth" (*adyādi*). The statement (*vākya*).
Having extracted the seed-syllable ending in the letter *va*, one should place *śiva* (the letter *ha*) upon it;

this is the most excellent and supreme *kūṭa*, the Great Mārtaṇḍabhairava.
Argha, obeisance! Flower, obeisance! Rhkṣrīṃ, obeisance to Śrī Mahāmārttaṇḍa Bhairava.

Bow down to that best of gurus, the venerable Kujeśa Bhairava, by whom this mandala has been truly blended with the fourfold reality.
The three gods.

Pādukā to Narāsanā. Pādukā to Mayūrāsanā. Pādukā to Mūṣāsanā. Aiṃ (5) Thrauṃ. Pādukā to the goddess Dambhakī of Prastaradvīpa and to the Kṣetrapāla Mahādhvāṅkṣa. Śrīṃ Hrīṃ. Pādukā to Kulaputra Vaṭukanātha. Gāṃ Gīṃ Gūṃ Gaḥ Glauṃ.
The sandals for the illustrious Kulagaṇeśvara; the sandals for the Yoginīs. To these, an offering (bali).

Aiṃ (5) Śhmraiṃ. To the goddess Amṛtadvīpasavarī, who is fond of Rati, the sandals for the Kṣetrapāla. (3) Oblation.

To the Power of the Support, the Sandal; obeisance to Anantāsana; obeisance to Kandāsana.

Salutation to the one seated upon the pericarp. Salutation to the one seated upon the lotus. Salutation to the one seated upon the crucible.
Meditative absorption.
O lady of beautiful countenance, her body is made of molten gold,
her face is exceedingly beautiful in the east, and she resembles a sapphire on the south.
To the west of the moon-faced one, who possesses the luster of snow, jasmine, and camphor, the northern direction is strewn with the radiance of rubies, equal in brilliance to the dawn. (2)
Thus ends the section on meditative concentration.
The worship.
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, the sandals of Avighnaśvara. Aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ āṃ, the sandals of Gaṇeśa.

The triple añjali; the shadow of nirvāṇa; the offering; you are the great offering.

To the lord of the Mahākaravīra cremation ground, accept the bali offering! Svāhā! Hskhphrīṁ, Siddhicāmuṇḍeśvarī, accept the bali offering! Svāhā! To all the sky-walkers and their retinues, accept the bali offering!
Svāhā! To all spirits, to all piśācas, and to all chosen deities...
Accept the offering, svāhā! [The rites beginning with] the invocation follow.
Gajamudrā. Incense.
Endowed with divine fragrance, bringing delight to all the gods— O all you gods, please accept this incense, which is a source of scent for you all.
O Maheśvarī, the Blessed One, who possesses universal form, is present among those who consume incense;
O Goddess of the Gods, may the Supreme Sovereign be well-pleased by this incense.
The lamp.
O Great Radiance, well-illumined and dispelling darkness on all sides,
may this lamp— light both external and internal— be accepted.
I shall show you the light.
O Supreme Goddess, please accept this divine food of great flavor, endowed with the six tastes, which has been offered by me with devotion.
The deluding karma.
O Goddess, please accept this food offering; grant me unwavering devotion, O Goddess, which removes untimely death and bestows the supreme goal in the hereafter.
Fruits, flowers, betel, incense, lamps, and this food offering—salutations!

Salutation to that illustrious Guru by whom that state was revealed, which is of the nature of an unbroken circle and by which the moving and the unmoving are pervaded.

One shall behold her with tawny eyes and red hair, uttering "kiṇi kiṇi," wearing a network of small bells, possessing a fierce nature yet removing all fears, holding a vessel in her hand, and making a roar;
she clearly utters the lion's roar: "la la la la la valaṃ varvvalaṃ," the very essence of the sky.
I bow to Kṣetrapāla, the lord of spirits, ghosts, and the like, who is encompassed by the multitude of planetary deities.
Clad in red garments, with a mass of matted locks blazing tawny,
fierce as a staff of lightning amidst a garland of flames,
he is fair with the golden luster of the rising sun.
I bow down to the great Vaṭukanātha, the son of Gaurī.

O Destroyer of the suffering of rebirth, who has stilled the fear of existence; to the one who puts an end to all obstacles, *gāṃ gīṃ gūṃ gai*! O you who hold the sword, who have gone to the Lord of the Sky (*Gaganapati*), who are the source of all accomplishments and all aims!
*Oṃ hrūṃ*, O you with the seal of the elephant-eye, who have gone to the wind of the *gasapa* [mantra], who abide alone upon the vehicle of the rat!
Oṃ hrīṃ hāṃ gāṃ! O Gaṇeśa, you who have two and a half faces, Lord of Obstacles, homage to you!
She who is Icchā, Jñānī, Kriyā, Sāsura, Varanā, Amitā, Śrī, Maṅgalā, Gaurī, Durgā, the Blessed One who bestows auspiciousness, Mātṛkā, and Carmamuṇḍā.
She is Brahmā, she is Viṣṇu, she is the entire host of planets and Bhairavīs, and she is the Kṣetrapālas;
she who possesses manifold forms and is endowed with various qualities and compassion—to her I bow.
Fair-complexioned, three-eyed, and radiant, he shines with five faces; seated upon a lion, he is the Attractor.
He holds a noose, a mace, a staff, a rosary, and the gesture of fearlessness; he is the Lord of Serpents, the Bestower of Boons.
His right hands hold a vessel filled with sweetmeats and the gesture of granting fearlessness, while his left hands likewise hold these.
Salutations to Helambanātha, who possesses a beautiful belly and a charming, protruding crest-lock.
Just as armor serves as a protection against weapon-strokes,
even so may peace serve as a protection against the ordinances of the Creator.
May the Kṣetrapālas of their respective abodes, together with Brahmāṇī and the others, along with Asitāṅga Mahābhairava,
Gaṇa, Vaṭuka, Yoginīs, and Kṣetrapālas, together with their limbs, hosts, and retinues, and the world-protectors beginning with Indra in the various directions,
being well-pleased, grant boons to the patron and his family and retinue.
May there be long life, health, sovereignty, progeny, wealth, fortune, and the increase of one’s lineage; may [the deities] become bestowers of the fruits and boons as declared in the scriptures.
There is no other refuge; you alone are my refuge. Therefore, O Supreme Goddess, protect me, protect me with your compassionate nature!
From the southern shadow. For the purpose of paying homage.
Worship of the retinue; the shadow of the pledge; the libation.
To the body of delusion, svāhā! To the body of the dog, svāhā!
She is both one and many, the sovereign of the three worlds;

the Blessed One is like the sky, the mistress of the earth and the lord of the quarters. She is the Mistress of the South, inaccessible through [ordinary] knowledge, the Mistress of the Earth, and the leader of the directions from the West, presiding over the assembly of Kula.
I bow to the auspicious Vāmā, the mother of the universe, the sovereign of the New Moon, who bestows spiritual accomplishments.
O Sacrificer, cause us to attain our own glory; may we be complete in every limb.
O Mother, the primordial state is the Blessed Lady whose essence is consciousness;
likewise, knowledge and will manifest in many ways as the triad of Hari, Hara, and Brahmā,
as well as the radiant Bhairava and the fivefold Śrī Yoginīs, who possess the luster of a lotus.
May the Moon, the Sun, the six rays, the stainless one, and Mars protect me eternally.

Sālāṅasaphayā, Mohanī, Suhlesadeva, and Nekumiyāke.

Having seen the peak, which is the drop of the moon at the end of dissolution, holding a white lotus and flowing with streams of milk, one constantly burns away a lineage of sins as vast as Mount Meru.
Dudu.
With milk as pure as nectar, which constantly flows from the wish-fulfilling cow and fills the earth, I bathe [the deity] by the command of Śiva.
Having maintained [it].
Always and perpetually bathe the god Umāpati, the beloved of the gods; thus the deities will always be well-pleased.
Ghera.
O Pinākinī, you whose banner is purified by clarified butter and whose phallus is pure;
O Śivā, who possesses the form of fire and serpents, [protect] the practitioner of Tantra.
Who is this?
Through this bath, one obtains the Gomukhī, which is produced by Śakti, beloved by the gods,
and a wish-fulfilling tree for all desires.
Sākhala.
This sugar-candy is of great flavor and is always cooling to the mind;
O God, this unbroken moon-shaped candy, when bathed [with water], bestows undivided strength.
The five nectars.

combined with the five substances and using the five limbs [of the ritual].

The attendant.
Divine sandalwood from Śrīkhaṇḍa, rich in fragrance and captivating to the mind—
may this sandalwood, adorned upon that which is called the forehead, be accepted.
Anointed with sandalwood paste, it is meritorious, pure, and a destroyer of sins;
it constantly removes calamities and bestows fortune, sovereignty, and happiness.
Siddhara.
Vīreśvarī, the Great Heroine, the Goddess who attracts the three worlds, is adorned with the ashes of heroes and is most excellent, crimson as vermilion.
Unbroken.
O Goddess, grant me this unimpaired and inexhaustible boon according to my desire, which bestows the accomplishment of Dharma, Kāma, and Artha, as well as supreme attainment in the next world.
View.
In those eyes wide with the vision of meditation, playful yet possessing the gaze of heroes,
the stainless eye is the world of the moon, sun, and fire, free from all unevenness.
The performers of sacrifice.
The sacred thread, the supreme purifier, which was born together with Prajāpati in the beginning—
may that life-prolonging, unaging, and brilliant sacrificial thread be the highest splendor for you.
Or else, [the door].
O Supreme Goddess, accept this most excellent ornament for the body of a deity, adorned with various garments made of fine linen and cotton.
In the Caphumāḍha [region].
O Lord of Gods, by the gift of this divine parasol, which is like a wish-fulfilling gem and shines like the full moon, grant me the fruit I have desired.
Bathing.
O auspicious lady, this supreme offering of flowers— consisting of various fragrant blossoms and the blooming of jasmine— is the bestower of good fortune and success.
The five banners.
This five-colored banner, made of fine linen, which hangs down from both ears and consists of the essence of the five elements, bestows these five [benefits].
The Ear-flag.
O Supreme Lord, accept this banner known as "Karna," which has the luster of pure vermilion, is four-cornered, and is most beautiful.
In all these places, there is the scent of cloth; the Japa and worship are performed with garlands.

Argha, obeisance! Flower, obeisance! Rhrkṣrīṁ, obeisance to Śrīmārttaṇḍabhairava!

The Guru is Brahmā, the Guru is Viṣṇu, the Guru is the divine Maheśvara;
the Guru is the entire universe—salutations to that illustrious Guru.

Salutations to the supreme gurus. Salutations to the gurus who dwell in the highest abode. To the sandals of the supreme teacher-guru, the illustrious Ādideva, [I offer] this oblation. Then follows the ritual placement (nyāsa). This is the Vatīśī nyāsa.
Aiṃ (5) Kiṇi (2) Vicce Koṅkaṇāyai Hraḥ Astrāya Phaṭ.
The purification of the hand. (4)

Aiṁ (5) *namo bhagavati hṛtkamalāyai* hrāṁ, salutation to the two thumbs (*aṅguṣṭha*). Aiṁ (5) *hsphreṁ kubjikāyai kuladīpāyai* hrīṁ, salutation to the two index fingers (*tarjanī*). Aiṁ (5) *hrāṁ hrāṁ hruṁ varvarashikhāyai* hrūṁ, salutation to the two middle fingers (*madhyamā*). Aiṁ (5) *ghore aghore aghorāmukhi*.
To Vahurūpā, Hraṃ, salutation to the two ring fingers. Aiṃ (5) Cchāṃ Cchīṃ, to Mahantārikā, Hrauṃ, salutation to the two little fingers.
Aiṁ (5) Kiṇi (2) Vicce Koṅkaṇāyai Hraḥ. Salutation to the two sides of the back of the hand. Thus is the ritual placement on the hands (karanyāsa).
Aiṃ (5) Homage to the Blessed One, to the Lotus of the Heart; homage to the venerable Upper Face. Aiṃ (5) Hsphreṃ;
homage to Kubjikā, the Lamp of the Kula, to the venerable Eastern Face. Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ;
homage to Varvarashikhā, to the venerable Southern Face. Aiṃ (5) Ghore Aghore Aghoramukhi...

Salutation to the many-formed Śrī Uttaravaktra (the Northern Face). Aiṃ (5) Chāṃ Chīṃ, salutation to Mahantārikā, the Śrī Paścimavaktra (the Western Face). Aiṃ (5) Kiṇi (2) Vicce, salutation to Koṅkaṇā, the Śrī Parāparavaktra (the Face that is both Supreme and Non-supreme). Thus is the ritual placement of the faces (vaktranyāsa).

Aiṁ (5) *Namo bhagavati hṛtkamalāyai* hrāṁ *hṛdayāya namaḥ*. Aiṁ (5) *Hsphreṁ kubjikāyai kuladīpāyai* hrīṁ *śirase svāhā*. Aiṁ (5) *Hrāṁ hrīṁ hruṁ varvvaraśikhe* hūṁ *śikhāyai vaṣaṭ*. Aiṁ (5) *Ghore aghore aghorāmukhī bahurūpāyai* hraiṁ *kavacāya huṃ*. Aiṁ (5) ...
Cchāṃ Cchīṃ, obeisance with Vauṣaṭ to the three eyes of Mahantārikā. Hrauṃ.
Aiṃ (5) Kiṇi (2) Vicce Koṅkaṇāyai Hraḥ Astrāya Phaṭ. Thus is the ritual placement on the limbs (aṅganyāsa).
The worship of the water vessel.

Salutation to the seat of the water-vessel (*jalapātrāsana*). Aiṁ (5) HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ, salutation to the sandals of the venerable Śrī Jalapātra-bhaṭṭārikā, the sovereign of the heroes and the power of bliss (*ānandaśakti*), who is the lord of the Bhairava of bliss, [represented by] ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ. Hrīṁ, [salutation] to the heart, and so forth. [Perform] the invocation (*āvāhana*) and other rites. [Display] the cow-mudrā (*dhenumudrā*). [Recite] the Gāyatrī.
Aiṁ (5). We know Kubjikā; we meditate upon her who is the lamp of the Kula; may that Kubjī inspire us. [This is] the sprinkling of all substances, beginning with the self.
The worship of the argha vessel: the sandals for the seat of the argha vessel.

Aiṁ (5) Hrāṁ Hrīṁ Hruṁḥ Prasphura (2) Ghora (2) Tarataru (2) Rupacata (2) Pracaṭa (2) Kaha (2) Vama (2) Dama (2) Ghātaya (2) Vighātaya (2) Vighni Hūṁ (2) Phaṭ Kroṁ Śrīmahākaumārikā Vicce Pādukāṁ. Hrīṁ to the heart, and so forth.
One should display the five mudrās.
Purification of the Elements (Bhūtaśuddhi): Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphreṃ Hsauṃ Hsauṃ Hsphreṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Aiṃ.
Self-worship: Aiṃ (5) Hskṣmlvryūṃ Śkṣmlvryīṃ, to the self, Aiṃ, sandalwood and sandals.

Hrīṃ, the sandals of unbroken grains; Śrī Vīrabhasma, the sandals of the ashes of the Hero; Hsphreṃ, the sandals that enchant all people; Hsauṃ, the sandals of various umbrellas, ornaments, and flowers. One should sprinkle water from the *argha* vessel upon the head. Aiṃ Kusauṃ, the sandals. (3)
Invocation.
Within the mandala of the venerable Samvarta, the power of bliss is established through the sequential steps; it is most formidable.
Therein is the fourfold emanation according to the rule, followed by another fivefold group situated in Akula and Kula, and then a sixfold group.
Then there are four, another fivefold group, and again four; such is this mandala.
May Śrī Kujeśa bow to that excellent Guru, Bhairava, by whom [all things] are intermingled.
I shall summon this; I summon.
(5) Ḍlaṃ, the sandals of Ādideva, the glory of the infinite maṇḍala; the sandals for Narāsana.
The sandal for the peacock posture.

Pādukā for Mūṣāsanā. Thrauṃ! Pādukā for the goddess Prastaradvīpadambhakī and the Kṣetrapāla Mahādhvāṅkṣa. Śrīṃ Hrīṃ! Pādukā for Kulaputra Vaṭukanātha. Gāṃ Gīṃ Gūṃ Gaḥ Glauṃ! Pādukā for Kulagaṇeśvara.
This is their offering (*bali*). [Perform] the invocation (*āvāhana*) and so forth. [Display] the *tarjanī* and *daṇḍagaja* mudrās. Thus is the worship of the three deities.
Now follows the worship of the retinue.

Aṃ, Brahmāṇī, the sandals for Asitāṅga Bhairava; Kaṃ, Māheśvarī, the sandals for Ruru Bhairava; Caṃ, Kaumārī, the sandals for Caṇḍa Bhairava; Ṭaṃ, Vaiṣṇavī, the sandals for Krodha Bhairava; Taṃ, Vārāhī, the sandals for Unmatta Bhairava; Paṃ...

To Indrāyaṇī, to Kapālibhairava, [I offer] the sandals (pādukā). Yaṃ, to Cāmuṇḍā, to Bhīṣaṇabhairava, [I offer] the sandals. Śaṃ, to Mahālakṣmī, to Saṃhārabhairava, [I offer] the sandals. To these, [this is] the bali offering.
The Seat: Homage to Ādhāraśakti; homage to Anantāsana.
Homage to the one whose seat is the bulbous root. Homage to the one whose seat is the fruit. Homage to the one whose seat is the leaf.
Salutation to the one whose seat is the filaments. Salutation to the one whose seat is the pericarp. Salutation to the one whose seat is the lotus.
The sandals for the seat of the preta.
Meditative absorption.
Aiṃ (5). Possessing a form at will and great splendor, with the brilliance of the sun at the end of an eon;
divine, resembling liquid lac, and possessing a radiance equal to a ruby.
Ambikā, whose limbs are variegated with all kinds of jewels, has assumed a formidable form;
she is four-armed and three-eyed, holding a trident, a rosary, and [the gesture of] recitation.
The Goddess, bearing the bindu upon the letter *kā*, is adorned with various jewels;
one should meditate upon the Great Goddess and worship Kuleśvarī.
Thus is meditation.
The triple añjali gesture.

Aiṃ (5) In the Śrī Anādimahāpīṭha, the great field of Meru, in the Kaula abode, HSKHPHREṂ Kubjikā, HSKṢMLVRYAṂ, the sandals of the venerable Śrī Kulacakreśvaranātha Ambā. Aiṃ (5) In the Śrī Anādimahāpīṭha, the field of Meru, in the Kaula abode, ŚKHPHRĪṂ Kubjikā, ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ, the venerable Śrī Kulacakreśvarī.
Mother, the sandal! (3)
The *vali*, the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*), and the *gāyatrī*: *aiṃ* (5) *kubjikāyai vidmahe* and so forth.
Aiṃ (5). Aghore Hrāṃ, Thaghore Hrīṃ, Ghoraghorantare Hrūṃ Phreṃ, Sarvataḥ Sarva Sarve Hraṃ Juṃ Saḥ, Hrāṃ Rūdrarūpe Hraḥ—[I worship] the sandals.
Aiṃ (5) Aiṃ Vajrakubjinīnī Hsphreṃ Trailokyākarṣaṇī Hrīṃ Kāmāṅgadrāvaṇi Klīṃ Strīṃ Mahākṣobhakāriṇi Aiṃ Sauḥ Saḥ Pādukāṃ.

Aiṁ (5). Homage to the Blessed One, Hsphreṁ, to Kubjikā! Hrāṁ hrīṁ hrūṁ! O Terrible One, O Not-terrible One, O You Whose Face is Not-terrible! Cchāṁ cchīṁ! Kiṇi (2)! Vicce! [I offer] the sandals! The offering!
Aiṃ (5). Worship of Gaṇeśa with the root mantra of the imperishable [deity] and the *gvākha* [mudrā].
Aiṁ (5) Hrāṁ Hrīṁ Hrūṁ, the sandals to Śikhāsvachanda Bhairava; [offering of] bali.
Worship of Indra and the other [deities].
Homage to Indra. Homage to Agni. Homage to Yama. Homage to Nairṛti. Homage to Varuṇa. Homage to Vāyu. Homage to Kubera. Homage to Īśāna. Homage to Ananta.
Oṃ, homage to Brahmā.
This is the offering for them.
The worship with the oblation of liquor.
Salutation to the one whose seat is a man. Salutation to the one whose seat is a swan. Salutation to the one whose seat is a bull.
Salutation to the peacock-throne. Salutation to the eagle-throne. Salutation to the buffalo-throne.

Salutation to Gajāsana (the Elephant Seat). Salutation to Pretāsana (the Corpse Seat). Salutation to Narāsana (the Human Seat). Aṃ, to Brahmāṇī and Asitāṅgabhairava, the sandals. Kaṃ, to Māheśvarī and Ruru Bhairava, the sandals. Caṃ, to Kaumārī and Caṇḍabhairava, the sandals. Ṭaṃ, to Vaiṣṇavī and Krodhabhairava.
Pādukā! To Vārāhī and Unmattabhairava, pādukā! Paṃ! To Indrāṇī and Kapālīśabhairava, pādukā! Yaṃ! To Cāmuṇḍā and Bhīṣaṇabhairava, pādukā! Śaṃ! To Mahālakṣmī and Saṃhārabhairava, pādukā!
This is their offering.
The sandals for the Kṣetrapāla of Prayāga; the sandals for the Kṣetrapāla of Varuṇa; the sandals for the Kṣetrapāla Kolākṣa.
The sandals for Aṭṭahāsa Kṣetrapāla; the sandals for Jayantī Kṣetrapāla.
The sandals for Caritra Kṣetrapāla; the sandals for Ekāmra Kṣetrapāla.
To the Kṣetrapāla of Devīkoṭa, [offer] a sandalwood slipper. With this, [present] the bali offering.
In the center of the eight-petaled [lotus], perform the worship with three añjalis.

Oṃ hrāṃ hrūṃ hṛtsaiṃ kusaṃnadīpajayabhadrakṣetrapāla mṛgā devī kṣroṃ, [offer] the sandals to the great Svasthāna Kṣetrapāla. (3) Vali. In the center. The mudrās for invocation and so forth. Thus ends the worship with the metal *vali* offering.
Three *añjali* gestures; the invocation and so forth; the *yonimudrā*; the *bali* offering.
Having looked down upon the world of men.
Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ! All the primary seats (pīṭhas) and secondary seats (upapīṭhas), as well as the gates and sub-gates.
The fields, sub-fields, and great assemblies are situated in every direction and region.
The yoginīs and the lords of the heroes of yoga have all assembled there;
this is the great wheel of the festival, and Śrīnātha is the bestower of boons upon me.
O Goddess, for those devotees who are intent upon the worship of the Guru’s feet according to the teaching,
may your grace, which bestows all accomplishments, always be theirs.
O Goddess, those on the surface of the earth who hate heroes and yoginīs— having offered them as a bali-oblation, you [consume them] at the immovable meeting-place of the *samaya*.
May she, who is surrounded by hosts of Yoginīs, cut away the hearing, memory, mental nourishment, flesh, fat, bones, and life-force of the wicked.
May those [deities] crowded with hosts of Yoginīs cut away the cries of "kuhuṃ," bad dreams, evil omens, and the double-tongued speech of the wicked.
Those three essences which are proclaimed to be present within the syllables beginning with Oṃ—
the collections of medicinal herbs and minerals— are found throughout the cardinal and intermediate directions.
In the great earth, the netherworld, the cosmic egg, and in all other places,
the practitioner whose self is united with yoga dwells eternally as a Yoginī.
The heroic deeds of the lords of the gods are true; the deities, the Siddhas, the Putrakas, the Ācāryas, and the Sādhakas abide for him who lies upon the earth.
Whether in a city or a village, in a forest or by a great river,
at a pond, a well, or a solitary tree, or in a cremation ground or a circle of Mothers.
May those who assume various forms, as well as the diverse spirits born from banyan trees—
all of them being fully satisfied— accept the offering from every side.
Even though I have come to them for refuge, all this shall bear fruit;
whatever action I have protected, whatever I shall do, and whatever has been done.
May they, being well-pleased by the offering of oblations and flowers, be mindful of me;
may all my actions be successful and may all my faults be pacified.
"I bow to the venerable letter Ku, who bestows the power of Śiva. Thus [is the offering of] the *samayabali*.
The triple añjali; the six limbs; the offering; the shade of nirvāṇa.
The great lineage of the Tvaṣṭṛs.
KṢĀṂ KṢĪṂ KṢŪṂ! O Kṣetrapāla, accept this bali-offering, svāhā! ŚRĪṂ HRĪṂ! O Kulaputra Vaṭukanātha, accept this bali-offering, svāhā! GĀṂ GĪṂ GŪṂ GAḤ GLAUṂ!
O Śrīkulagaṇeśvara, accept this bali-offering, svāhā!

HŪṂ! To the lord of the Mahākaravīra cremation ground, accept this bali offering, svāhā! HSKHPHRĪṂ! To the illustrious Siddhicāmuṇḍā, accept this bali offering, svāhā! To Ākāśacarī and all the [deities] of the eight directions, accept this bali offering, svāhā! To all spirits, to all piśācas, to all...
Accept the offering (bali) from the chosen deities, svāhā! [Perform] the invocation and so forth; [form] the yoni-mudrā.
Incense.
Endowed with divine fragrance, bringing delight to all the gods— O gods, please accept this incense, which is the very scent of all the deities.
O Goddess, when the Blessed One, the Great Sovereign who possesses all forms, partakes of the offerings of incense,
may the Supreme Goddess be well-pleased by this incense.
The lamp.
O one of great splendor, this lamp, brilliantly radiant and dispelling the darkness everywhere, is a light for both the exterior and the interior; please accept it.
I shall show the light.
The Sālāṅga, Saphayā, Mohanī, Devayā, and Havanetaya [are] the garlands for worship.
The food offering.
O Supreme Goddess, please accept this divine food of great flavor, endowed with the six tastes, which I have offered with devotion.
O Goddess, please accept this food offering; grant me unwavering devotion.
O Goddess, [grant] the removal of untimely death and the supreme goal in the hereafter.
Fruit, flowers, betel, incense, lamps, and this food offering—salutations!
Recitation.
thrauṁ svāhā (10) || śrīṁ hrīṁ svāhā || (10) || yāṁ svāhā ||
YHMKHPHRĀṂ SVĀHĀ (54) || ŚMKHPHRĪṂ SVĀHĀ (54) || NIRVVĀNAYĀ ||
For you, for protection; [this is] the hymn of praise.
Salutations to that glorious Guru, by whom that state was revealed— the state which is of the form of an unbroken circle and by which all that is moving and unmoving is pervaded.
The Glorious Saṃvartā.
The tawny-eyed one with red hair, with the sound "kiṇi kiṇi," possessing a white network of small bells,
with fangs and a mouth of cruel nature, who removes all fear, holding a vessel in hand and making a roar—
a clearly manifest lion’s roar, "la la la la la"— the power of auspiciousness, the reality of space.
I bow to the Kṣetrapāla, the lord of spirits, ghosts, and the like, who is saluted by the hosts of planetary deities.
Clad in red garments, with a mass of flaming tawny matted locks,
bearing a fierce trident wreathed in garlands of fire,
he is as radiant as gold at sunrise.
I bow to Vaṭukanātha, the son of Gaurī.
O destroyer of the suffering of the ṛṣis, O remover of fear and disease, O you who bring an end to all obstacles!
Gāṃ gīṃ gūṃ gaiṃ! To Khaḍga, to Gaṇapati, to the one who has gone to the sky, for the sake of the attainment of all goals and purposes!
Oṃ hrūṃ glūṃ! O you who possess the trunk of a mudrā-elephant, who move with the speed of the wind, who reside alone upon the vehicle of a rat;
oṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ hāṃ gāṃ! O Gaṇeśa, who are the lord of the twice-born, the sun, and the hosts, obeisance to you, the Lord of Obstacles!
She is Icchājñānī, she is Krīyā, she is the one saluted by the best of Asuras; she is known as Śrī, Maṅgalā, Gaurī, Durgā, the Blessed One who bestows auspiciousness, Mātṛkā, and Carmamuṇḍā.
She is Brahmā and she is Viṣṇu; she is the entire host of planets, Bhairavī, and the Kṣetrapālas;
she is manifold, possessing many forms and various qualities of grace—O Yoginī, I bow to you.
The Brahmāṇīya [Sūtra].
She is the Vedic hymns, the Brahmasāvitrī, and the revealer of the reality of Brahman;
she is four-armed, four-faced, and devoted to the four Vedas.
Although she has four arms, she is devoted to the four yugas;
seated upon a celestial chariot drawn by swans, the Grandmother (Pitāmahī) possesses a gentle form.
Holding a book and a rosary in her hands, and granting boons and fearlessness,
the goddess has yellow flowers as her favorite, a yellow body, and is clad in yellow garments.
Satisfied by yellow offerings, anointed with yellow perfumes,
residing at the foot of an Udumbara tree, dwelling in the sacred field of Prayāga, eternally established in the eastern seat— O Brahma-śakti, salutations to you!
Belonging to Maheśvara.
The Great Goddess Māheśvarī, the stainless Mohamāyā,
is mounted upon a great bull and resounds with the great sound of "Huṃ."
His body resembles a golden face; he holds a skull, the crescent moon, a trident, a three-eyed [face], a rosary, and a water-pot.
Adorned with ornaments of bone upon all her limbs, she grants boons with her right hand;
the sovereign of the gods, she pervades all things—creation, maintenance, and destruction.
The goddess is devoted to white flowers; she has a white body and wears white garments, clad in white cloth and adorned with ornaments of pearls.
O Māheśvarī, who dwells in the Tāla tree at the great field of Vārāṇasī and resides in the southeastern seat— homage be to you!
Belonging to Kaumārī.
In the state of Vāla, she is Mahāraudrī Kaumārī, with blood-red eyes,
clad in red garments, and her body is as crimson as vermilion.
Four-armed and auspicious, she holds a cord of power and a vessel of accomplishment;
she is the supreme maiden, whose vehicle is the excellent peacock.
The goddess who delights in red flowers, who dwells in blood, flesh, and fat,
who is to be worshipped with jujube fruits in the great field, and who resides in the banyan tree.
O Kaumārī, who always resides on the southern seat, salutations to you!
O Vaiṣṇavī...
She is Vaiṣṇavī, the illusory power of Viṣṇu, the destroyer of the formidable fortresses of the Daityas;
her body is greenish-blue in hue, and she is seated upon Garuḍa.
Holding a conch, a discus, and a mace in her hands, she is adorned with four arms;
she is the great sport of blazing jewels, embellished with various gems.
Always bearing green flowers and fragrance,
she remains present in her form throughout heaven, the mortal world, and the netherworld.
Residing in the Kadamba tree in the great field of Aṭṭahāsa, you dwell in the Nairṛta seat; O Nārāyaṇī, salutations to you!
Of Vārāhī.
Vārāhī has a terrifying red body, red hair, and a large belly;
she is deep-seated with fearsome fangs, and her eyes possess the brilliance of the rising sun.
She is adorned with a garland of skulls and a wreath beautified by various flowers;
she is mounted upon a great buffalo and possesses a radiance equal to a blazing fire.
Adorned with fish, goads, and flaying knives, and decorated with ornaments of human bone,
she has three eyes and a blazing body, destroying the pride of the wicked.
O Jayantī, who dwells in the sacred field, who takes refuge in the nimba tree,
who is eternally established on the Nāga-pīṭha in the form of a boar— salutations to you!
The verses dedicated to Indra.
She is Śakreśvarī, the thousand-eyed one, her body reddish like saffron;
she is Sureśvarī, the goddess who is everything, adorned with all ornaments.
The four-armed, large-eyed goddess, holding a parasol and a bell, is the wielder of the great vajra; she stands upon the elephant Airāvata.
The goddess delighted in various flowers, adorned with various jewels,
her limbs anointed with various perfumes, and resplendent in various garments.
O Śakreśvarī, who dwells in the Kadamba tree in the great field of Caritra and resides eternally upon the Vāyu-pīṭha; salutations to you!
To Cāmuṇḍā.
Cāmuṇḍā, Caṇḍikā, Caṇḍī, Caṇḍacaṇḍā, Sudhāriṇī,
Caṇḍāṭṭahāsā, Caṇḍākṣī, Pracaṇḍā, and Caṇḍahāsinī.
With fangs formidable, red eyes, tawny hair, and a sunken belly;
with slender limbs, terrifying, fierce, and frightening with her lolling tongue.
Mounted upon a great preta, her eight arms are most beautiful;
her hands hold a sword and shield, and she bears a hand-drum and a khaṭvāṅga staff.
The Goddess has a skull-bowl in her hand, is adorned with the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness,
wears a human skin, and stands upon the hide of a tiger at her waist.
The Goddess wears a garland of skulls and is adorned with ornaments of bone;
her limbs are decorated with ornaments of human bone, and she always delights in wine and meat, O Beloved.
In every single pore of his body, he appeared like a thousand suns;
his form was wreathed in garlands of flames, possessing a radiance equal to ten million lightning bolts.
She is the retinue consisting of bhūtas, vetālas, and ḍākinīs, as well as the rākṣasī;
she dwells in the aśvattha tree within the great sacred field of Ekāmraka.
Salutation to Cāmuṇḍā, whose limbs are situated in the north on the pedestal.
Belonging to Mahālakṣmī.
Mahālakṣmī, the Great Goddess, the beauty of the gods in her auspiciousness,
is seated upon a lion throne, mounted on sandals made of lapis lazuli.
Four-armed and large-eyed, she holds a sword and a shield;
she is adorned with anklets, necklaces, and armlets, and wears jeweled earrings.
Her entire body was inlaid with jewels, adorned with a crest-jewel,
and she was arrayed in garments of various flowers and gems, along with perfumes and unguents.
The Goddess pervades the three worlds; she dwells in all that exists, both moving and unmoving.
She is bowed to by the Siddhas and Gandharvas, and is worshipped by the Vidyādharas and gods.
O Great Plakṣa tree of Devīkoṭa, following the lineage of the eight families of withdrawal;
salutations to you, Mahālakṣmī, who reside in the seat of Īśāna.
By means of the middle [wheel].
Homage to Cakreśvarī, who is red in color, four-armed, holding a rosary and a trident, and with a skull and a dot in her hands.
O Goddess who dwells in the eight fields, who resides in the eight trees,
who is joined with the eight Bhairavas, O Mother of the eight— salutations to you!
The Mother of all beings, the illuminator of all principles,
the Goddess who removes all defects, and the severer of the bonds of saṃsāra.
You alone are the embodiment of all scriptures; you alone are the form of Yoga;
you alone are creation and dissolution; you alone are the form of sustenance.
You alone possess all forms; you alone are the one whose form is the universe.
[I bow to] the Lord of the Sacred Seats, the Great God, the God of gods, the Great-Souled One.
Terrible, fearsome, fierce, and ghastly, she possesses a profound form;
her body resembles blue collyrium, and she has a massive frame during the great festival.
Adorned with various arms, bearing various scriptures, and auspicious;
O Three-eyed One of great splendor, possessing a radiance equal to fire and the sun.
With eyebrows arched like the line of a forest fire in brilliance,
he holds a trident, a skull, a khaṭvāṅga staff, a hand-drum, a raised index finger, and a banner.
Or else, she is auspicious, wearing a tiger-skin garment and a sword;
[he is] the God holding a noose, a goad, a vajra, a spear, and a mace.
She holds a skull-bowl, a flaying-knife, and a wheel, and is draped in an elephant hide;
her face is terrifying with protruding fangs, and she is girt around the waist with a tiger skin.
Her entire body adorned with ornaments, she is beautified by human bones as her flowers;
the God wears a garland of heads and holds a skull-cup, the most excellent of garlands.
She whose crest-jewel is of great splendor, who holds a skull as her moon-ornament,
and who eternally dances upon the seat of a great corpse— then she is indeed my beloved.
Her entire body is the splendor of the crescent moon, resembling a mass of matted hair and lapis lazuli;
she dwells eternally upon the four seats, residing in the eight sacred fields.
O Dear One, the Goddess resides in the eight forms; O Bhadrakālī, you are eternally established upon the auspicious throne, surrounded by the sixty-four Yoginīs.
Obeisance to you, Vīrabhadra, the creator of auspicious causes;
and to Asitāṅga, Ruru, Caṇḍa, and Krodhabhairava.
Unmattabhairava, Kapālibhīṣaṇa, and likewise the eight Saṃhāras— O you who are the eight Bhairavas, salutations be to you!
Each possessing its own station, authority, essential form, and power,
they abide in their respective duties within the divine realms and upon the earth.
To the Kṣetrapālas in the ten directions, to the fourteen fields,
and to the fifty Kṣetrapālas— to you, the Kṣetrapāla, obeisance!
Salutations to you, the Lord of Lords, the Great Lord, the Primordial Lord, the Great-Souled One, the Glorious Lord,
the Lord of Siddhis, and Mīnanātha.
Obeisance to you, the Lord of the Field, the Lord of the Pīṭha, the Great-Souled Lord of the Lamp, the Lord of the Pretas, the Bhūta, and Vaṭukanātha.
Salutations to you, the Lord of three, the Lord of nine, the supreme Lord of sixteen, the twenty-seven, the fifty-two, and the eighty-four.
O Lord of all the Siddhas, for the increase of the lineage and the family, you are the purity of yoga and the supreme radiance; salutations to you who are all that.
The man who recites it once, twice, or thrice a day, or who repeats it a hundred times—he attains the supreme; listen!
She destroys grief and anxieties; she destroys the deities of obstacles;
she destroys quarrels among people; she destroys those who partake in suffering.
It shall destroy fear and poverty; it shall eliminate even the most excellent of enemies;
it shall extinguish fire and thieves; and it shall dispel the wrath of kings.
It shall destroy terrible, venomous [spirits] and destroy all malevolent afflictions;
it increases longevity, health, sovereignty, wealth, and grain.
May there be dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa; supreme fame and good fortune; prosperity, accomplishment, glory, and wealth; and the infinite expansion of learning and wisdom.
And through the good friend of intelligence and wisdom, your growth increases day by day;
it shall always destroy the timely impurities of the infinite one during their arising.
All the worlds will bow down [to them], and long life shall be obtained.
Thus ends the hymn on the descent of the sacred seats (*pīṭhāvatāra-stotra*), as remembered by the Goddess from the *Śrīpīṭhanirṇaya*.

In the center is the Goddess Pretāsinī, the beautiful one dwelling upon the sacred seat (pīṭha), whose limbs are red, who holds a trident and a skull-topped staff in her hands, and who bestows the essence of worldly existence.
I perpetually bow my head to that Goddess, who is worshipped at all times by Brahmā, Upendra, Surendra, and the hosts of Kinnaras, and who bestows the attainment of all desires and goals.

The Yoginī stands in the sacred field (kṣetra), surrounded by Brahmāṇī and others such as Jayā; she is in a state of aesthetic equilibrium (samarasa) with all the Śrī-Vīras and the gods, holding a trident and a rosary.
Unmattā holds the auspicious weapon along with the Sāṅka, and she is enveloped in streams of nectar.
May the Mistress of the Wheel (Cakreśvarī), accompanied by the first drop that obscures passion and the rest, protect you!
Just as armor serves as a defense against the strikes of arrows,
even so may peace serve as a defense against the afflictions ordained by fate.
May the guardians of the respective sites, beginning with Brahmāṇī accompanied by Asitāṅga Mahābhairava,

along with the Gaṇas, Vaṭukas, Yoginīs, and Kṣetrapālas, together with their limbs, retinues, and attendants, and the world-protectors such as Indra in the cardinal and intermediate directions, be well-pleased and grant boons to the patron.

May there be an increase in lifespan, health, sovereignty, progeny, wealth, fortune, and lineage for [the names] together with their attendants and retinues; may they be granters of boons according to the fruits declared in the scriptures.
There is no other refuge; you alone are my refuge.
Therefore, O Supreme Goddess, protect me, protect me with your compassionate nature!

The shadow at the time of agreement; the shadow of one's own right side; for the sake of prostration.
Statement: Regarding the deity of Mohanī, [it is] the one who has come from the sacrificer; regarding the counting of the Mohanīs, [they are] one or many.

O Blessed One, you are the single form manifested manifoldly in the world; you are the Sovereign Lady in the east, the Mistress of Beings in the north, like the sky in the west, and the Queen of Night in the south.

I bow to the venerable Vāmā, the mistress of the new moon, the mother of the universe, the bestower of spiritual accomplishments, who is inaccessible to mere intellect, the sovereign of Kula, the leader of the beautiful hosts of Kula, and the mistress of the eastern quarter.
O dog, you have come to the end.
O Mother, the first step is the Blessed One whose nature is consciousness;
then Jñāna and Icchā in abundance, followed by the triad of Hari, Hara, and Brahmā;
then the five radiant Bhairavas, and thereafter the five Śrī Yoginīs.
May the Moon, the Sun, and the six pure rays protect me constantly; may Mars [protect me] as well.
The dissolution of the maṇḍala; the dismissal of the deities; the dismissal of the offerings; and the establishment of the witnesses.
Thus ends the ritual procedure for the worship of the pedestal in the illustrious *Madhya*.
The back-offering (*piṭhipūjā*) is performed by means of the *dhunakāvavaya* [chant] at the residence of the patron (*yajamāna*), together with the *svastika* and the *savidyāvaka*.
May Vighna always grant well-being; may Mārtaṇḍa likewise grant well-being;
may all the Yoginīs grant well-being; and may the Pīṭhas of one’s own field grant well-being.
In the east, south, west, north, above, and likewise below—
these six deities, established in the Āgamas, are both hidden and manifest.
Bhairava and Bhairavī, together with their limbs, may they grant well-being;
they abide in their own wheel, accompanied by their own mantras, their own mudrās, and their own weapons as attendants.
May those situated in the planets, lunar mansions, and zodiac signs grant well-being for the welfare of all;
may the heroic Pramelās and the leaders of the hosts of Yoginīs grant well-being.

May there be well-being, O Goddess, Sovereign of the Gods; may the King of Mantras be ever-present. May the sacrificial fires and the deities of the lineage be satisfied with the offerings of grain and oblations;
may there be well-being for the king and his subjects, and may there be well-being for the sacrificer at all times.
Like a man, at each step, he went toward the single-plank boat.
For the sake of pleasing Śrī Ākāśamahābhairava, the installation of a chariot for the patron, the Mānavagotra Śrī Śrī Jayabhūpatīndramallavarman,
followed by the hoisting of a golden pinnacle and banner upon it, and a thousand oblations of Bhairava-fire performed day and night.

O you who dwell upon the earth, in the heavens, in the intermediate space, and in the depths of the netherworld, may those various forms of yours perish by the command of Śiva.
The lamp.
"Brilliantly luminous, of great splendor, dispelling darkness everywhere—this lamp, a light both internal and external, is offered; please accept it."
For the sake of bending the palm trees.

Hrāṃ, svāhā to the principle of the self (ātmatattva). Hrīṃ, svāhā to the principle of knowledge (vidyātattva). Hrūṃ, svāhā to the principle of Śiva (śivatattva), together with the principle of the Guru. By means of the three principles. (3)
At that time, for the worship of the pedestal, there was a bath; [this was] for the purpose of bathing and adorning [the deity].

The syllable *ū* is the seed-syllable of Vāyu; above that is Varuṇa, and above him is Vajrapāṇi; above that is Kāla joined with the final letter of the alphabet; above that is the supreme seed-syllable of Fire (*ra*) together with *sa*;
[then] the Moon (*a*), the Bindu (*m*), and the end of dissolution (*visarga*); [this whole] holds a white lotus and flows with streams of milk.
For having seen this sin, which is like Mount Meru, it constantly consumes the entire family.
Sandalwood.
May this divine sandalwood paste from Śrīkhaṇḍa, rich in fragrance and most enchanting,
which adorns the forehead, be accepted.
Anointed with sandalwood paste, it is meritorious, pure, and a destroyer of sins;
it constantly removes calamities and bestows fortune, sovereignty, and happiness.

Vīreśvarī, the Great Heroine, the Goddess who attracts the three worlds, is adorned with the ashes of heroes and is most excellent, glowing red like vermilion.

It fulfills all aims and purifies with curd; it is entirely like the full moon. It destroys the flood of sins and the flood of misfortunes, and it brings about the accomplishment of desired objects. From it arises prosperity that grants victory and bestows great wealth and success.
May Śambhu, who possesses long life and is ever victorious in his eternal activity, protect you all.
The deluding [karma].

She who fascinates the three worlds, who burns the families of enemies, who shatters all obstacles, and who completely removes the fear of *bhūtas*, *pretas*, and *piśācas*; she who destroys the *ḍākinīs*,
who protects all beings and humans, who is the mouth of Śiva and the totality, and who is endowed with every auspiciousness.
That Goddess, who bestows all prosperity, is endowed with the threefold gait of Mohanīya.
O dogs, you who follow the sacrificer!

One should meditate upon Jāgeśvara, who is fair-complexioned, possessing three eyes, five faces, and seated upon a lion; he performs the act of attraction and holds a noose, a mallet, a staff, a rosary, and the gesture of fearlessness;
he is dark-brown, holds a vessel filled with sweetmeats, and bestows fearlessness with his right and left hands respectively.
Salutations to Helambanātha, who possesses a charming crest-jewel and a well-proportioned belly.
Brahmāṇī, whose face is as gentle as the lotus and the moon; Māheśvarī, who by her playfulness [destroys all]; Kaumārī, who destroys the pride of enemies; Vaiṣṇavī, whose weapon is the discus;
Vārāhī, whose mouth makes a deep and terrible gurgling sound like a cloud; and Aindrī, whose weapon is the thunderbolt.
May Cāmuṇḍā, Gaṇanātha, Bhairava, and the hosts of Mothers protect me.
Homage to you, Cakreśvarī, who is red in color, four-armed, holding a rosary and a trident, and with a skull and a drop in her hands.
Sepha.
You are established in divinity; with a firm foundation, you pervade the three worlds.
You accept this presence for the sake of the prosperity of the sacrificer and others.
May there always be prosperity for the bipeds, and likewise may there be prosperity for the kingdom;
may this son, born of the sacrificer, be endowed with excellent offspring, cattle, and kinsmen.
Protect us at all times; O Bhairava, homage be to you!
May they be well-established and granters of boons. Thus is the consecration of the parched grains.

May Bhairava, seated upon a corpse-throne, pleased and the remover of the fear of worldly existence, whose form is the mantra;
may Caṇḍī, fierce and seated upon a throne; may the guardians of the world, the lords of serpents with their hoods expanded;
may the Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, Daityas, together with the hosts of Pitṛs, the Mothers, and the protectors of the Kṣatriyas [grant protection].
May the yoginīs, joined in yoga, drink this nectar that moves upon the water and within the sky.
May all the deities, the Rudras, the Vināyakas, the Yoginīs, and the Kṣetrapālas who are established within my body drink [of this].
Homage to the venerable Lord!
Homage to Siddhinātha; homage! Homage again and again to Śrī Kujeśanātha!

O Goddess, whose single form is manifold in this world; O Sovereign Lady in the east; O Mistress of Beings in the north; O Goddess who is like the sky in the zenith; O Blessed One, the Mistress of the south; O Goddess inaccessible to knowledge in the southwest; O Mistress of the earth in the west; O Leader of the quarters in the northwest; O Goddess of the waters in the north; O Mistress of the directions in the northeast.
I bow to the auspicious Vāmā, the mother of the universe, the sovereign of the New Moon, the bestower of spiritual accomplishments.
O Mother, the first position consists of the Blessed One whose nature is consciousness; then follows the triad of Hari, Hara, and Brahmā, along with Marīci;
thereafter the five radiant Bhairavas, and then the five Śrī Yoginīs.
May the Moon, the Sun, and the sixfold rays, together with the pure Mars, protect me eternally.

In the year 821, on the thirteenth day of the dark fortnight of Phālguṇa, on this day, the illustrious Śrī Ākāśamahābhairavasaraṭha [was established] by the lineage of the illustrious Śrī Śrī Jayabhūpatīndramalladeva. May there be auspiciousness!
(1) On this day, etc. For the sake of the Mānava-gotra sacrificer, the illustrious Śrī-Jayabhūpatīndramalladeva-varman, with the desire to please his chosen deity (*iṣṭadevatā*),
for the purpose of the consecration and entry into the new house, [this] *siddhāgni* [rite], the sacrifice of ten thousand oblations (*ayutāhuti*), and the nine pedestals (*navapīṭha*)...
